title: Weight-Space Programming for THOX Edge Models: Evidence Review, Small-Scale Recreation, and a Signed Patch Channel
read_level: full (v1.1.0 PDF downloaded from Zenodo API on 2026-11-25 and read with pdftotext)
metadata_mismatch: Record page for 23954378 lists files under record 23955394 (v1.1.0; report states DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23955394). The version read is v1.1.0, which says E1-E4 results are carried over from v1.0.0. Authors are affiliated with THOX.ai (company).
why_wsp: Industry technical report reviewing the Takehi et al. WSP claims, re-verifying the released Qwen3.5-0.8B edit, running small-scale read/write/fix/audit recreations with deterministic tools (not an LLM editor), and specifying a signed weight-patch distribution channel.
domain: edge LLM deployment (ThoxEdge-0.8B, a Qwen3.5-0.8B derivative); small control/RL networks; patch distribution
editor: none (deterministic tools); quote: "The reader, writer and editor in these experiments were deterministic tools, not a frontier API model" (Sec 4)
target: trained small networks (E1, 30 networks); hand-built paddle controller (E2); MountainCar policy with 747 weights (E3); 2-layer 4-head transformer, 70,656 parameters (E4); re-verification of released Qwen3.5-0.8B edit
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: E3: "It touches 16 of 747 weights (2.14%)" (Sec 4.3); released Qwen edit: 130,188 changed entries (executive summary)

headline_results.quote: The released edit rebuilds bit-exactly (130,188 entries, both hashes).
The MATH-500 gain was re-run once in full on Hugging Face Jobs: 51.0% for the edited model

headline_results.claim: Scripted, LLM-free pipeline reproduces similar edit
headline_results.quote: a scripted pipeline with no LLM re-derived a similar edit in about five CPU minutes

headline_results.claim: E1 read: only composed reader works
headline_results.quote: R4 scores 100%, with its permutation control at chance
As a paddle controller it catches 100% of balls in the standard regime and 92.1% in a hard regime.
raises success to 92.8% over 512 episodes; a random edit of the same size scores 0% at every gain

headline_results.claim: E4 audit negative: planted behaviour never formed
headline_results.quote: after 1,400 steps the loss on repeat positions was 3.19 against 3.18 elsewhere.
An exact patch therefore ships the factor plus a sparse residual: 80.6 KB for both tensors.

cost.quote: a scripted pipeline with no LLM re-derived a similar edit in about five CPU minutes

baselines_and_controls: permutation control (E1), gradient-trained oracle (E2), same-size random edit (E3), third-party thinking-off baseline (46.8% vs 50.6%, cited not measured); pre-registered decoding-control comparison specified but not completed
runs_and_variance: E1: "10 seeds per task, every network at 100% task accuracy"; MATH-500 re-run once; E3 over 512 episodes; no variance reported in captured text
robustness_of_edits: Quantization of patches stated as open; planned E5 gate requires keeping at least 80% of bf16 effect at Q4_0 (not run)
verification: hash and bit-exact rebuild of released edit; Ed25519-signed patch manifests; Rust unit tests 3/3, bit-identical apply, rollback, tampered-manifest rejection (Table 5)
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a (no LLM editor run); notes a scripted LLM-free pipeline reproduces much of the Takehi loop-suppression edit
limitations_stated: Source is an unreviewed blog post; E1-E4 carried from v1.0.0 and not re-run; small-scale only; no frontier-editor runs; decoding-control measurement stopped by compute billing (HTTP 402); safety risks include refusal removal and patch channel as attack surface.
code_or_data: Zenodo artifact thox-wsp-v1.1.0-artifact.zip (record 23955394); private dataset Thox-ai/thox-wsp-evals
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 blog (Sparks of WSP)
notes_for_survey: Replication/evaluation-style industry report: independently rebuilds and re-runs the Takehi Qwen3.5-0.8B edit (51.0% vs reported 48.1%) and flags that the thinking-off decoding comparison is unresolved. Its own recreations use deterministic tools rather than an LLM editor; proposes gating weight patches behind decoding controls and a signed patch format.
